options: A. Unplug the tool (or lock out the power switch) before touching the blade or chuck, wear safety glasses and hearing protection, inspect wood for nails or loose knots, and use a push stick to keep hands clear of the blade.
B. Leave the machine plugged in with your finger off the trigger while wrenching the arbor nut, and wear loose knit gloves to guide wood within an inch of the saw blade.
C. Remove the blade guard permanently so you can see the pencil line better, and reach behind a spinning table saw blade to pull off scrap pieces.
D. Stand directly in line with the table saw blade without eye protection so you can hold the board down if it starts to kick back.

pamphlet_excerpts: Timber is grown, harvested, and milled: Then workers called buckers lop off the limbs and slice the trunks into shorter lengths (logs) that are easier to handle (p. 14).
Timber is grown, harvested, and milled Principle 2: The logs are trucked, floated, or carried on railroads to asawmill (p. 14).
Timber is grown, harvested, and milled Principle 3: At the mill, logs are debarked (their bark is removed), and saws cut them into boards (lumber) (p. 14).
Timber is grown, harvested, and milled Principle 4: Small logs are often cut into boards in a single pass through a set of saws (a gang saw) that makes many cuts at once (p. 14).
step_by_step_procedure: Step 1 (Timber is grown, harvested, and milled): Large logs may make several passes through one saw (a headsaw) that slices off a board at a time until the whole log is cut into lumber (p. 14).
Step 2 (Timber is grown, harvested, and milled): The new lumber, called green lumber, is edged and trimmed to straighten the sides and cut into boards of standard lengths (p. 14).
Step 3 (Timber is grown, harvested, and milled): Lumber is graded for quality, appearance, and strength (p. 14).
Step 4 (Timber is grown, harvested, and milled): Manufacturers use them to make flooring, pallets, and similar products (p. 14).

Step 2 (Working Drawings of A Project): Step 2 (Make working drawings of a project): Think of "tenant", someone who dwells inside a place, to help you remember that the tenon (the peg) goes inside the mortise (the hole) (p. 62).

Step 3 (Working Drawings of A Project): Step 3 (Make working drawings of a project): For requirement 6, you might choose aproject below, take an idea from a book or website listed in the resources section, or think (p. 62).

options: A. Unplug the tool (or lock out the power switch) before touching the blade or chuck, wear safety glasses and hearing protection, inspect wood for nails or loose knots, and use a push stick to keep hands clear of the blade.
B. Leave the machine plugged in with your finger off the trigger while wrenching the arbor nut, and wear loose knit gloves to guide wood within an inch of the saw blade.
C. Remove the blade guard permanently so you can see the pencil line better, and reach behind a spinning table saw blade to pull off scrap pieces.
D. Stand directly in line with the table saw blade without eye protection so you can hold the board down if it starts to kick back.
